passages.title: Dialogue between a mother and her son
passages.instructions: Complete the dialogue between a mother and her son. Choose the son’s correct answers from the choices given (A–D).
paragraphs: Mother: Where is the key of my car?
Mother: But it is not there! Didn’t I give it to you?
Mother: So where did I put it?
Mother: But that cannot be. I came here in my car.
Mother: You are right.
Choices given: A. May be you left it at your office.  B. So let’s look for it in the kitchen.  C. I don’t know. You usually put it in your bag.  D. No, you didn’t. I have just come from the shop.

passages.title: The two farmers
passages.instructions: Read the story and answer the questions (41–50) according to the information in the story.
paragraphs: Long time ago, an old farmer was travelling to a town very far from his village. On his way, he met another young farmer. He was also travelling to the same town and they agreed to go together.

The old farmer was talking about himself all the way to the town. He said, “I am a [line 5] great man. I am the bravest and the strongest in my village. A few weeks ago, I killed a lion with my bare hands. I have also done many great things. I am also very wise. I am the wisest man in our village. The king always asks me for advice.”
The young farmer listened to him but said nothing. They travelled together for hours. They were both hungry and tired, so they went into a small hotel to eat some food.

[line 10] The waiter came and said, “Welcome gentlemen. We have very good food today.” They both told him to bring the food. The waiter brought the food and the old farmer began to eat first. The food was too hot that tears came to his eyes.

“Why are you crying, my friend?” asked the young farmer. He was ashamed to tell the truth, so he told a lie instead. He said, “I was thinking of my poor brother. The people [line 15] of my village killed him last week. They said that he was a thief, but this was not true. I am crying because I thought of him suddenly.”

“I am sorry to hear that,” said the young farmer. “I am sure he was a good man.” Then he began to eat. The soup was so hot that he also began to cry. The old farmer saw the tears in his eyes and asked him, “Why are you crying?”
[line 20] “My friend,” answered the farmer, “I am crying because you were not killed instead of your brother!”
passages.note: The paper gives no title. Line numbers (5–20) as printed.

questions.stem: Dialogue, gap (1). Mother: “Where is the key of my car?” Son: “______” Mother: “But it is not there! …”

options.A: May be you left it at your office.
options.B: So let’s look for it in the kitchen.
options.C: I don’t know. You usually put it in your bag.
options.D: No, you didn’t. I have just come from the shop.

explanation_steps: The son does not know, but he names a place: “You usually put it in your bag.”
The mother’s next words “But it is not there!” refer to that place (the bag).
Textbook: English Grade 8, Unit 1 (p. 1–21): conversations.
questions.explain_simple: He says: I don’t know, it is usually in your bag. She answers: it is not there.
tips: “there” in the next line points back to a place in the answer.

similar_questions.stem: Where are my glasses?  ______  But they are not there!
explanation_steps: “there” = on the table.

textbook_ref.rule: In a dialogue, the answer must fit the question before it AND the line after it.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, Unit 1 (p. 1–21): conversations

questions.stem: Dialogue, gap (2). Mother: “But it is not there! Didn’t I give it to you?” Son: “______”

options.A: May be you left it at your office.
options.B: So let’s look for it in the kitchen.
options.C: I don’t know. You usually put it in your bag.
options.D: No, you didn’t. I have just come from the shop.

explanation_steps: She asks if she gave him the key. He says no and explains why: he has just come from the shop.
Textbook: English Grade 8, Unit 1 (p. 1–21): conversations.
questions.explain_simple: No, you didn’t – I was at the shop.
tips: A yes/no question → an answer with Yes/No.

similar_questions.stem: Didn’t you take my pen?  ______

options.A: No, I didn’t. I was outside.

explanation_steps: No + reason.

textbook_ref.rule: In a dialogue, the answer must fit the question before it AND the line after it.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, Unit 1 (p. 1–21): conversations

questions.stem: Dialogue, gap (3). Mother: “So where did I put it?” Son: “______” Mother: “But that cannot be. I came here in my car.”

options.A: May be you left it at your office.
options.B: So let’s look for it in the kitchen.
options.C: I don’t know. You usually put it in your bag.
options.D: No, you didn’t. I have just come from the shop.

explanation_steps: The son guesses a place: “Maybe you left it at your office.”
The mother says that cannot be, because she drove home (so the key came with her).
Textbook: English Grade 8, Unit 1 (p. 1–21): conversations.
questions.explain_simple: He guesses: the office. She says no, she drove home with it.
tips: The next line (“I came here in my car”) answers the guess.

similar_questions.stem: Where did I leave my bag?  ______  No, I didn’t go to school today.
explanation_steps: The next line rejects the guess ‘school’.

textbook_ref.rule: In a dialogue, the answer must fit the question before it AND the line after it.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, Unit 1 (p. 1–21): conversations

questions.stem: Dialogue, gap (4). Mother: “But that cannot be. I came here in my car.” Son: “______” Mother: “You are right.”

options.A: May be you left it at your office.
options.B: So let’s look for it in the kitchen.
options.C: I don’t know. You usually put it in your bag.
options.D: No, you didn’t. I have just come from the shop.

explanation_steps: The key must be in the house, so the son suggests: “let’s look for it in the kitchen.”
The mother agrees: “You are right.”
Textbook: English Grade 8, Unit 1 (p. 1–21): conversations.
questions.explain_simple: He suggests looking in the kitchen. She agrees.
tips: Let’s … = a suggestion.

similar_questions.stem: We can’t find the ball.  ______  Good idea.
explanation_steps: suggestion.

textbook_ref.rule: In a dialogue, the answer must fit the question before it AND the line after it.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, Unit 1 (p. 1–21): conversations

additional_textbook_refs.rule: Use polite forms for requests (Can/Could I …?), apologies (I'm sorry …) and advice (You should …).

questions.stem: There is ______ man in the house. I don’t know him.
explanation_steps: The speaker does not know the man, so he is not a known man → a man (not the).
man begins with a consonant sound → a.
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 74; English Grade 8, p. 56–58, 204.
tips: a/an = not known / first time.

similar_questions.stem: There is ______ dog in our garden. Whose is it?
explanation_steps: unknown → a.

textbook_ref.rule: Use 'the' for a thing that is the only one (the moon, the sun) or already known; a/an for one thing that is not specific.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 74; English Grade 8, p. 56–58, 204

questions.stem: The nurse is my ______. Everyone likes him.
explanation_steps: “him” shows the nurse is a man → brother.
Textbook: English Grade 6, p. 61; English Grade 7, p. 7–8.
tips: Use the pronoun as a clue.

similar_questions.stem: The doctor is my ______. She works in Keren.
explanation_steps: She → aunt.

textbook_ref.rule: Use an object pronoun (me, him, her, us, them) after a verb or preposition; possessive pronouns (mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs) replace a noun.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 6, p. 61; English Grade 7, p. 7–8

questions.stem: Ali was singing when Sara ______ in the wedding party.
explanation_steps: Both actions were going on at the same time in the past → past continuous: was dancing.
“dances” and “is dancing” are present; “dancing” alone is not a verb.
Textbook: English Grade 6, p. 175–176.
questions.explain_simple: Past, at the same time → was dancing.
tips: Two long past actions at the same time: was … -ing.

similar_questions.stem: I was reading while my brother ______.
explanation_steps: was sleeping.

textbook_ref.rule: Past continuous = was/were + verb-ing; it shows an action that was going on at a time in the past.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 6, p. 175–176

questions.stem: ______ can I visit my uncle?
explanation_steps: The sentence asks about a time to visit → When.
What/Which need a noun or object; Why does not make sense here.
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 100–101.
tips: When = time.

similar_questions.stem: ______ can I see the doctor? – At 3 o’clock.
explanation_steps: time.

textbook_ref.rule: Question word + auxiliary + subject + verb (Why did you travel?). Short answers repeat the auxiliary: Yes, you can.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 100–101

questions.stem: The students ______ test next Monday.
explanation_steps: next Monday → will have.
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 20, 175.
tips: future → will + verb.

similar_questions.stem: We ______ a holiday next week.
explanation_steps: will have.

textbook_ref.rule: Future: will + base verb (I will go) or am/is/are going to + base verb.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 20, 175

questions.stem: My sister came to school ______ Wednesday.
explanation_steps: day → on.
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 12; English Grade 8, p. 31, 181.
tips: on + day.

similar_questions.stem: The shop is closed ______ Sunday.
explanation_steps: on.

textbook_ref.rule: Travel: by car/bus/plane; time: at 5 o'clock, on Monday, in June; place: in, on, under, between, next to.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 12; English Grade 8, p. 31, 181

questions.stem: ______ she is his neighbour, he doesn’t know her name.
explanation_steps: Neighbour but doesn’t know her name → contrast in one sentence → Although.
Textbook: English Grade 8, p. 30, 68, 82, 98–99.
tips: Although + clause, clause.

similar_questions.stem: ______ it was cold, he went swimming.
explanation_steps: contrast.

textbook_ref.rule: because + reason; so that + purpose; but/however + contrast; and + addition; so + result.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, p. 30, 68, 82, 98–99

questions.stem: How ______ children are there in the classroom?
explanation_steps: children → countable → How many.
Textbook: English Grade 6, p. 148, 274–276; English Grade 8, Units 6–7.
tips: How many + plural.

similar_questions.stem: How ______ teachers work here?
explanation_steps: many.

textbook_ref.topic: Quantity words (some, any, much, many, too, enough)
textbook_ref.rule: some = an amount with plural or uncountable nouns; too = more than is good; very = a lot; enough = as much as needed.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 6, p. 148, 274–276; English Grade 8, Units 6–7

additional_textbook_refs.rule: Question word + auxiliary + subject + verb (Why did you travel?). Short answers repeat the auxiliary: Yes, you can.

questions.stem: Question: ______  Answer: I think it was at 7 o’clock.
explanation_steps: “at 7 o’clock” is a time → When.
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 100–101.
tips: When → time.

similar_questions.stem: Question: ______  Answer: On Friday.
explanation_steps: time.

textbook_ref.rule: Question word + auxiliary + subject + verb (Why did you travel?). Short answers repeat the auxiliary: Yes, you can.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 100–101

questions.stem: A car is expensive ______ faster than a donkey.
explanation_steps: “expensive” is a bad point and “faster” is a good point → contrast → but.
Textbook: English Grade 8, p. 30, 68, 82, 98–99.
tips: but = contrast.

similar_questions.stem: The phone is old ______ it works well.
explanation_steps: contrast.

textbook_ref.rule: because + reason; so that + purpose; but/however + contrast; and + addition; so + result.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, p. 30, 68, 82, 98–99

questions.stem: Did you ______ your breakfast?
explanation_steps: did + base verb → eat.
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 72; English Grade 8, p. 7.
tips: did + base verb.

similar_questions.stem: Did he ______ the door?
explanation_steps: close.

textbook_ref.rule: Past simple: verb-ed or irregular past form; questions and negatives use did + base verb (Did he call?).
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 72; English Grade 8, p. 7

additional_textbook_refs.rule: Question word + auxiliary + subject + verb (Why did you travel?). Short answers repeat the auxiliary: Yes, you can.

questions.stem: Maths is not ______ English for me. I don’t have good result in the subject.
explanation_steps: The second sentence shows maths is hard for the writer.
“Maths is not as simple as English” = maths is harder. That fits.
“not harder than” and “not as difficult as” would mean maths is easier. “difficult than” is wrong grammar.
Textbook: English Grade 6, p. 58; English Grade 7, p. 16, 124; English Grade 8, p. 109.
questions.explain_simple: Maths is hard for me → not as simple as English.
tips: not as + adjective + as = less … than.

similar_questions.stem: I always fail science. Science is not ______ history for me.
explanation_steps: science is harder.

textbook_ref.rule: Long adjectives: more ... than / the most ...; short adjectives: -er than / the -est. 'not as ... as' means 'less ... than'.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 6, p. 58; English Grade 7, p. 16, 124; English Grade 8, p. 109

questions.stem: We sometimes ______ to the radio for the news.
explanation_steps: sometimes → habit; we → listen (no -s).
Textbook: English Grade 6, p. 57; English Grade 8, p. 7.
tips: I/you/we/they + base verb.

similar_questions.stem: They often ______ football.
explanation_steps: play.

textbook_ref.rule: Present simple: he/she/it takes -s (he watches); questions and negatives use do/does + base verb (Does he help?).
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 6, p. 57; English Grade 8, p. 7

additional_textbook_refs.rule: Adverbs of certainty: definitely = 100% sure; probably = nearly sure; maybe/perhaps = not sure.
additional_textbook_refs.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 56, 60–61; English Grade 8, p. 52

questions.stem: A donkey is not as big as an elephant. This means the same as:

options.A: A donkey is bigger than an elephant.
options.B: An elephant is bigger than a donkey.
options.C: A donkey and an elephant are not big.
options.D: An elephant is smaller than a donkey.

explanation_steps: not as big as → the elephant is bigger.
Textbook: English Grade 6, p. 58; English Grade 7, p. 16, 124; English Grade 8, p. 109.
tips: not as … as = less.

similar_questions.stem: A cat is not as fast as a horse. This means:

options.A: A horse is faster than a cat.

explanation_steps: horse faster.

textbook_ref.rule: Long adjectives: more ... than / the most ...; short adjectives: -er than / the -est. 'not as ... as' means 'less ... than'.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 6, p. 58; English Grade 7, p. 16, 124; English Grade 8, p. 109

additional_textbook_refs.rule: Check who does what, the tense and the comparison; the new sentence must say exactly the same thing.
additional_textbook_refs.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 16 (comparison); English Grade 8, p. 105 (be able to)

questions.stem: ______ tell me your name and then your age.
explanation_steps: “… and then …” shows an order of steps → First.
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 56, 60–61; English Grade 8, p. 52.
tips: Sequence words: first, then, next, finally.

similar_questions.stem: ______ wash your hands, then eat.
explanation_steps: first.

textbook_ref.rule: Sequence adverbials (first, secondly, then, next, finally) show the order of actions (English Grade 8, Unit 9).
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 56, 60–61; English Grade 8, p. 52

questions.stem: ______ pencil is this? Is it yours?
explanation_steps: Asking about the owner → Whose pencil?
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 100–101.
tips: Whose + noun.

similar_questions.stem: ______ shoes are these?
explanation_steps: owner.

textbook_ref.rule: Question word + auxiliary + subject + verb (Why did you travel?). Short answers repeat the auxiliary: Yes, you can.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 100–101

questions.stem: The farmer ploughed the land. The passive form of this active sentence is:

options.B: The land was ploughed by the farmer.
options.D: The farmer was ploughed by the land.

explanation_steps: Object (the land) → subject; ploughed → was ploughed; by the farmer.
Textbook: English Grade 6, p. 134; English Grade 7, p. 145; English Grade 8, p. 12.
questions.explain_simple: The land was ploughed by the farmer.
tips: Passive keeps the tense: past → was/were + past participle.

similar_questions.stem: Aster cooked the food. Passive:

options.A: The food was cooked by Aster.

explanation_steps: was cooked.

textbook_ref.rule: Passive = am/is/are/was/were + past participle (Cars are sold). Use it when the doer is not important.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 6, p. 134; English Grade 7, p. 145; English Grade 8, p. 12

questions.stem: Lewhat said, “She is excellent.” The correct indirect speech for the sentence is:

options.A: Lewhat said that she was excellent.
options.B: Lewhat said that she is excellent.
options.C: Lewhat said that I am excellent.
options.D: Lewhat said that you are excellent.

explanation_steps: “she” stays “she”; is → was.
Textbook: English Grade 8, p. 151, 174–175.
tips: Reported speech: present → past.

similar_questions.stem: Ali said, “He is my friend.”

options.A: Ali said that he was his friend.
options.B: Ali said that I am his friend.
options.C: Ali said he is my friend.

explanation_steps: is → was.

textbook_ref.rule: In reported speech after 'said', change the pronoun (I → he/she) and move the tense back (am → was, will → would).
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, p. 151, 174–175

questions.stem: A carpenter is a person ______ makes tables and chairs.
explanation_steps: person → who.
Textbook: English Grade 8, p. 115.
tips: who = people.

similar_questions.stem: A pilot is a person ______ flies planes.
explanation_steps: who.

textbook_ref.topic: Relative clauses (who, which, that, where, whose)
textbook_ref.rule: A relative clause starts with who (people), which (things), that, where (places), when (times) or whose (possession).
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, p. 115

questions.stem: Which of the following is correctly capitalised and punctuated?

options.A: Can Zahra read, write, speak and listen to English.
options.B: Can Zahra read, write, speak and listen to English.
options.C: Can Zahra read, write, speak and listen to English?
options.D: Can Zahra read, write, speak and listen to english?

explanation_steps: The sentence is a question (Can …?), so it ends with a question mark.
English is a language name → capital E. D has a small e.
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 58, 172; English Grade 8, Unit 2 and Unit 8 punctuation.
questions.explain_simple: A question ends with “?” and English has a capital E.
tips: Questions → ?; languages → capital letter.

similar_questions.stem: Which is correct?
explanation_steps: capital + ?

textbook_ref.rule: Names of people, places, days and months start with a capital letter; an apostrophe shows possession (Ali's) or a missing letter (don't).
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 58, 172; English Grade 8, Unit 2 and Unit 8 punctuation

questions.review_flag: Misprint: options A and B are printed identically (both end with a full stop). Answer C is not affected.

questions.stem: Is she ______ ride a bicycle?
explanation_steps: “Is she … ride” needs “able to”: Is she able to ride …?
“Is she can ride” is wrong (can makes its own question: Can she ride?).
Textbook: English Grade 8, p. 105.
questions.explain_simple: Is she able to ride? (not “Is she can”)
tips: be able to → Is she able to …? ; can → Can she …?

similar_questions.stem: Are you ______ swim?
explanation_steps: Are you able to …

textbook_ref.rule: 'be able to' means the same as 'can' (ability).
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, p. 105

questions.stem: If you are late, the teacher ______ angry.
explanation_steps: angry is an adjective, so it needs a verb “be”: will be angry.
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 161; English Grade 8, p. 34, 129.
tips: will + be + adjective.

similar_questions.stem: If you eat too much, you ______ sick.
explanation_steps: will be sick.

textbook_ref.rule: First conditional: If + present simple, will + base verb. Zero conditional (always true): If + present, present. Second: If + past, would + base verb.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 161; English Grade 8, p. 34, 129

questions.stem: Which of the following is not correct?
explanation_steps: “is climb” is wrong: we need “is climbing” or “climbs”.
B and C are correct. D is weak (better “a banana”), but A is clearly the wrong one.
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 39; English Grade 8, p. 7.
questions.explain_simple: “She is climb” is wrong. It should be “She is climbing”.
tips: is/are + verb-ing, never is + base verb.

similar_questions.stem: Which is not correct?
explanation_steps: is playing.

textbook_ref.rule: Present continuous = am/is/are + verb-ing, for actions happening now.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 39; English Grade 8, p. 7

questions.review_flag: D ‘She ate banana.’ is also not good English (missing ‘a’: ‘She ate a banana.’). A ‘She is climb the tree.’ is the intended wrong sentence. Teacher check.

questions.stem: ______ does a lion live?
explanation_steps: We ask about the place a lion lives → Where.
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 100–101.
tips: Where = place.

similar_questions.stem: ______ do fish live? – In water.
explanation_steps: place.

textbook_ref.rule: Question word + auxiliary + subject + verb (Why did you travel?). Short answers repeat the auxiliary: Yes, you can.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 100–101

questions.stem: The police ______ the thief.
explanation_steps: The police catch thieves → captured.
wasted does not fit; urgent is an adjective.
Textbook: English Grade 8, Appendix 1: Vocabulary list, p. 221–227.
tips: Choose the word whose meaning fits.

similar_questions.stem: The cat ______ a mouse.
explanation_steps: caught.

textbook_ref.rule: Read the whole sentence: the words before and after tell you the meaning of the new word.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, Appendix 1: Vocabulary list, p. 221–227

questions.stem: As table is to a carpenter, ______ is to a writer.
explanation_steps: A carpenter makes tables; a writer writes (makes) novels.
Textbook: English Grade 8, Appendix 1: Vocabulary list, p. 221–227.
questions.explain_simple: Carpenter makes a table; writer makes a novel.
tips: worker – thing he makes.

similar_questions.stem: As bread is to a baker, ______ is to a tailor.
explanation_steps: a tailor makes clothes.

textbook_ref.rule: Read the whole sentence: the words before and after tell you the meaning of the new word.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, Appendix 1: Vocabulary list, p. 221–227

questions.stem: Which of the following has correct spelling?
explanation_steps: Correct: choice, tough, cancel, symbol. Only “cancel” is right.
Textbook: English Grade 8, p. 72–95 (spelling: doubling letters, dropping 'e').
tips: choice, tough, symbol are Grade 8 vocabulary words.

similar_questions.stem: Which has correct spelling?
explanation_steps: relax.

textbook_ref.rule: Learn the spelling of common words; the sound /s/ at the end of a word is often spelt -ce (justice, office).
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, p. 72–95 (spelling: doubling letters, dropping 'e')

questions.stem: Our school garden is very beautiful. It ______ a lot of people.
explanation_steps: Beautiful things make people want to come and look → attracts.
Textbook: English Grade 8, Appendix 1: Vocabulary list, p. 221–227.
tips: attract = pull people towards it.

similar_questions.stem: The new park ______ many visitors.
explanation_steps: attracts.

textbook_ref.rule: Read the whole sentence: the words before and after tell you the meaning of the new word.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, Appendix 1: Vocabulary list, p. 221–227

questions.stem: There is a rapid increase of students in the school. It has doubled in recent years. What is the opposite of rapid?
explanation_steps: rapid = fast. The opposite is slow.
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 222; English Grade 8, p. 160.
tips: First find the meaning, then the opposite.

similar_questions.stem: What is the opposite of ancient?
explanation_steps: modern.

textbook_ref.topic: Opposites and words with the same meaning
textbook_ref.rule: A synonym has the same meaning (hit = strike); an opposite has the reverse meaning (happy – sad).
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 222; English Grade 8, p. 160

questions.stem: In which order would the following words be written in a dictionary?
explanation_steps: di- before dr-: distance (dis), divide (div) → s before v.
dr-: draw (a) before drink/drive (i); drink (n) before drive (v).
Order: distance, divide, draw, drink, drive.

tips: Second letter i comes before r.

questions.stem: Which animal is more expensive than a donkey?
explanation_steps: Donkey 3000 Nakfa; cow 5000 Nakfa → the cow costs more.
Textbook: English Grade 8, Unit 6 (p. 120–141): graphs and data.
questions.explain_simple: A cow (5000) costs more than a donkey (3000).
tips: more expensive = higher price.

questions.explain_simple: A dog looks after our houses and is free.
tips: Both parts must be true.

questions.stem: A ______ is the least expensive of all animals.
explanation_steps: least expensive = cheapest. A dog is free (0 Nakfa), cheaper than a hen (150).
Textbook: English Grade 8, Unit 6 (p. 120–141): graphs and data.
questions.explain_simple: A dog is free. It is the cheapest.
tips: least expensive = cheapest; free = costs nothing.

questions.stem: A ______ has two legs and is used for its meat.
explanation_steps: A hen has two legs (the others have four) and gives meat.
Textbook: English Grade 8, Unit 6 (p. 120–141): graphs and data.
questions.explain_simple: A hen has two legs and gives meat.

questions.stem: A cow is more useful than a dog because ______

options.A: it protects our animals from hyena and fox.
options.B: it gives us milk to drink and meat to eat.
options.C: it helps to look after our animals and houses.

explanation_steps: The table: a cow gives milk and meat. A and C are the uses of the dog.
Textbook: English Grade 8, Unit 6 (p. 120–141): graphs and data.
questions.explain_simple: A cow gives milk and meat.
tips: Match the animal to its own row.

similar_questions.stem: A donkey is useful because it ______
explanation_steps: carries goods and fetches water.

questions.stem: Which of the following sentences is false?

options.A: People use a donkey to protect their homes.
options.B: People use a cow for food.
options.C: All the animals have different uses.

explanation_steps: The dog protects homes; the donkey carries goods. So A is false.
B true (milk and meat). C true (each animal has its own list of uses).
Textbook: English Grade 8, Unit 6 (p. 120–141): graphs and data.
questions.explain_simple: A donkey carries goods; it does not protect homes. A is false.
tips: Test each sentence with the table.

questions.stem: The two farmers were travelling:
explanation_steps: “He was also travelling to the same town and they agreed to go together.”
Textbook: English Grade 8, reading lessons (e.g. Unit 10, p. 199–220: stories).
questions.explain_simple: They went to the same town.
tips: Find the words of the options in the text.

similar_questions.stem: Where did the farmers eat?
explanation_steps: a small hotel.

questions.stem: The old farmer did not say one of the following:

options.A: He was the wisest man in his village.
options.B: He was the bravest man in his village.
options.C: He was the king of his village.
options.D: He was the strongest man in his village.

explanation_steps: He said he was the bravest, strongest and wisest, and that the KING asks him for advice.
He never said he was the king. → C.
Textbook: English Grade 8, reading lessons (e.g. Unit 10, p. 199–220: stories).
questions.explain_simple: He said the king asks him for advice; he did not say he was the king.
tips: “did not say” – find the one missing from the text.

similar_questions.stem: What did the old farmer say he killed?
explanation_steps: a lion.

textbook_ref.rule: Find the part of the text with the same words as the question; read that sentence carefully.

questions.stem: The word “bare hands” (line 6) means:
explanation_steps: “I killed a lion with my bare hands” = only with my hands, no knife or spear → without a weapon.
Textbook: English Grade 8, Appendix 1: Vocabulary list, p. 221–227.
questions.explain_simple: Bare hands = only hands, no weapon.
tips: bare = with nothing on or in it.

similar_questions.stem: He walked on the hot sand with bare feet. ‘Bare feet’ means:
explanation_steps: no shoes.

questions.stem: The word “they” (line 11) refers to:

options.A: the two farmers and the waiter

explanation_steps: “They both told him (the waiter) to bring the food.” → they = the two farmers.
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 7–8 (pronouns).
questions.explain_simple: The two farmers asked the waiter for food.
tips: “him” here is the waiter, so “they” are the others.

similar_questions.stem: “The boys met the teacher. They greeted him.” ‘They’ =
explanation_steps: the boys.

questions.stem: Tears came to the eyes of the farmers because …

options.B: they were angry with one another.
options.C: they were angry with the people.
options.D: the old farmer’s brother was killed.

explanation_steps: “The food was too hot that tears came to his eyes.” and “The soup was so hot that he also began to cry.”
Textbook: English Grade 8, reading lessons (e.g. Unit 10, p. 199–220: stories).

questions.stem: The word “him” (line 15) refers to:
explanation_steps: “I was thinking of my poor brother. The people of my village killed him last week.” → him = the brother.
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 7–8 (pronouns).
tips: Read the sentence before.

similar_questions.stem: “My dog was lost. We found him near the river.” ‘him’ =
explanation_steps: the dog.

explanation_steps: suddenly = quickly and without warning.
Textbook: English Grade 8, Appendix 1: Vocabulary list, p. 221–227.
tips: suddenly ↔ slowly.

similar_questions.stem: The rain started suddenly. ‘Suddenly’ means:
explanation_steps: quickly.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not true about the story?

options.C: The young farmer ate before the old farmer.

explanation_steps: “the old farmer began to eat first.” So the young farmer did NOT eat before him. C is not true.
Textbook: English Grade 8, reading lessons.
questions.explain_simple: The old farmer ate first. C is not true.
tips: first / before / after – read carefully.

similar_questions.stem: Which is not true?

options.C: The young farmer talked a lot.

explanation_steps: the old farmer talked a lot.

textbook_ref.rule: A 'true' statement must agree with the text in every part; the text may say it in other words.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, reading lessons

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the story?

options.A: Both farmers told the truth why they were crying.
options.B: Both farmers were crying because the food was too hot.
options.C: The two farmers were friends for a long time.
options.D: The old farmer’s brother was killed by the village people.

explanation_steps: The real reason for both was the hot food → B true.
A false (the old farmer lied). C false (they met on the way). D is only the old farmer’s lie.
Textbook: English Grade 8, reading lessons.
questions.explain_simple: Both cried because the food was hot.
tips: Don’t trust what a liar says in a story.

similar_questions.stem: Why did the young farmer say “you were not killed instead of your brother”?

options.A: to laugh at the old farmer’s lie

explanation_steps: He answered the lie with a joke.

textbook_ref.rule: A 'true' statement must agree with the text in every part; the text may say it in other words.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, reading lessons

questions.stem: Choose the best title for the story.

options.B: The rich and the poor farmers

explanation_steps: The story is about the old farmer and the young farmer.
The text says nothing about rich or poor; the waiter is a small part. → The two farmers.
Textbook: English Grade 8, Unit 10 (p. 199–220).
questions.explain_simple: The story is about two farmers.
tips: Title = the main people or the main event.

similar_questions.stem: A story tells how a boy and his dog find a lost child. Best title:

explanation_steps: whole story.
